claims.quote: We set a spare plank across the hearth and, with Rao watching every move, built a safe mock-up from the clockwork's visible parts.
The cam turned, the push-rod struck the plank with a dry, hard thud and a small split opened where the wood took the blow.

I picked up the flake of red sealing-wax from where I'd pocketed it. "This was on the mantel that morning," I said, and then, because the catalogue exists even when the files do not, I told them what evidence boards later confirmed: a matching impression had been found on a crate label in Derek's shed.

Next I set the brass plate where everyone could see the tiny nick. "I recognised this at once," I said. I told them how the nick is a maker's tic, the sort of filing mark a man leaves like a signature. Derek's hand went to his sleeve as if to cover a tool.

He lunged for the ashtray on the desk as if to throw it, a desperate gesture that was too late. Rao was quicker: a hand on his shoulder, a cuff on his wrist... "I was paid," he said. "Paid to take something and make it look like—like an accident. She was to be... silenced. There was a debt. I was told to fetch a page. I didn't mean—"
Henry rose but did not strike.
